project.title: The anti-metastatic effect of pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 inhibition in bladder cancer via p-AKT, p-ERK, p-Src and p-JNK pathway
project.projectDescription: To confirm the anti-metastatic effect in bladder cancer cell lines, the PDK4 gene was knocked down and phosphorylated protein changes were compared through LC-MS/MS analysis.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: bladder cancer cell pellets lysed and collected protein. For enzymatic labeling, peptide were labeled 18O labeling after in-solution trypsin digestion. The labeled peptide mixtures were enriched using TiO2 phosphopeptide enrichment and Clean-up kit (Thermo) refer to the manufacturer’s instructions. Additionally, for clean-up peptide, desalted through SDB and GC tips (GC Science, Tokyo, Japan) according to instruction manual. Peptide samples were analyzed on an UltiMate 3000 RSLC nano LC system (Thermo) coupled with an LTQ-Orbitrap mass spectrometer.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: The MS raw files were processed with MaxQuant (version 1.5.1.0) software against the UniProt Homo sapiens proteome database (2018). For the phosphoproteomics data, searched parameters were set as follows; 16O was set as light labels and 18O was set as heavy labels. Trypsin/P was chosen as protease and up to 2 missed cleavages were allowed. Variable modifications included acetyl (protein N-term), Oxidation (M) and phospho (STY). In addition, carbamidomethyl (C) was set as a fixed modification. Protein false discovery ratio (FDR) was set at 0.01. Using the iGPS 1.0 software, the kinase substrate phosphorylation network (KSPN) was constructed by submitting differentially expressed phosphopeptides.
